name: Machine Learning
description:
The first part of the course addresses discrete and computational structure. For instance, data may be given in terms of a relational structure like a graph. We will discuss different models, their expressive and learning abilities and distributional robustness. Next, there has been recent interest in using neural networks to help address difficult optimization tasks. We will discuss ways to combine learned models and optimization, for instance, endowing algorithms with predictions or making classical algorithms learnable, aligning neural networks and algorithms, and implications.
The second part of the course will address geometry. First, data may have specific structure, such as symmetries. We will discuss ways to respect such symmetries within neural networks, as well as their benefits and drawbacks. Symmetries also apply to the weights of neural networks; we will discuss implications and the idea of using neural network weights as data (weight space learning). Finally, geometry of the representations learned by a neural network affects its properties. We will discuss recent findings in this area, e.g., correspondences across models.

Content:
1. Learning and discrete structure
a. Neural models for graph-structured data, their capabilities and failures, theoretical properties
b. Methods for combining algorithms and neural networks, with examples
c. Training methods
d. Understanding neural networks via algorithms
e. Neural network/LLM reasoning and algorithms

2. Geometry and data: symmetries
a. putting symmetry into models: well-known models and general strategies
b. selected theory
3. Neural weight spaces and symmetry
a. Implications for neural networks
b. Weight space learning

4. Representation geometry
a. Exploratory studies
b. Steering representations
c. Correspondences across models
prerequisites: A graduate course in machine learning or deep learning; a course in algorithms; a course in Discrete Structures for Computer Science (e.g. IN0015 or a comparable course); basic linear algebra
